contribution: For analyses of how credit constraints and financial frictions amplify and spread macroeconomic fluctuations (the financial accelerator and credit cycles)
rationale: Recent prizes have covered banking crises (2022), labor history (2023), institutions (2024) and innovation-led growth (2025), so macro-finance frictions are an open area. Kiyotaki–Moore's 'Credit Cycles' (1997) and Gertler's financial-accelerator work have shaped post-2008 macro modeling and central bank practice, and these three are perennial top forecasts. Other strong contenders include Berry and Pakes (empirical IO), Blanchard (macroeconomics), and Manski or Hausman (econometrics). This is a forecast, not knowledge of the result.
